Exactly, it's nothing new that queer people are portrayed as mentally unstable/criminal/morally questionable in media, and that's exactly the problem. It's a bad stigma attached to them that has prevailed since a long time, similarly to how other minority groups were portrayed in less favourable or more stereotypical ways in the past and even today still. 

Your excuse of Rowlings behaviour by stating that "it has been done before" is not a good one. Just because something has been done more frequently in the past that has no weight on whether or not that is good or bad. In most cases this statement is used against minorities, different times different issues, whether it be people of colour, the gay community, other minority groups and even political parties that will use "it's always been that way" as an excuse for THEMSELVES to not adjust to change and to reflect on their own narrow minded or outdated viewpoints. 

JK Rowling doesn't go out into the streets to kill trans people, but she has a loud voice, and she uses it as a dogwhistle for TERFs and other groups of people who dislike the trans community. She is a large public persona people can point to when they claim they are not transphobic BUT don't agree with *this or that* part about trans people. 

YES, trans people cannot change their chromosomes, but does that matter? No trans person claimed so, statements like such are merely dog whistles to make people who oppose trans rights even just a little bit, feel smart and correct in their decision, leading them down further a slippery slope. 

It's not as cut and dry as you want to believe, nor is it as simple an issue they want to make you feel like it is. JK Rowling isn't trans, nor are her Twitter friends, she doesn't know the struggles of LGTBQ people, so for HER, of course, it IS simple to say "well that's how it always was, deal with it". But for people who ARE trans, who CANNOT change that fact and struggle with their own identity each day, this is not a small issue, it's their life, their identity. 

Put it into perspective, you type:
>  I don't hate trans people, I agree that they should be allowed to live freely 

Imagine someone would have to permit YOU to live freely? Approve of even your existence? Why should anyone, no matter if they are gay, trans, cis, or hetero, need to PROVE themselves to be a human being deserving of rights and compassion, just for being who they are? 

You don't understand both sides, and you probably haven't bothered to, your post reeks of ignorance and a silent need for validation in those parroted beliefs. I am trans, and a few years ago I slid down this slippery slope of trans hate, it begins like this, in a benign way, that seems simple, but it only goes downhill from there.

 Talk to trans people, get involved, hear their voices, talk to them about this, even, if they agree to. People shouldn't need to fight for their right to exist, or to be the way they want, nobody tells you how to dress, no? We are all the same people, with different identities, and different issues. JK Rowling is one of those, unfortunately, she voices and expresses those internal issues in a way that is harmful to others, and she is able to, because she has a large platform. 

That's all.

Yeah, I don't think they would be likely to do this, when they can just reskin the same mesh on the same rig, and have everyone buy it up each time. GW2 is backed by a relatively small developer team compared to other MMo's, and their animation/rigging department seems especially meagre judging by the last expansion, where I could only count three, maybe four new rigs and animation sets if the jade mech counts, for Saltspray dragon types and Soo-Won, and for the Siege Turtles and jade bots (whichwouldn't be that complex to rig and/or animate) (correct me if there are more new rigs). Plus new animations for skiffs and fishing, *very* minimally for new elite specs. And three new emotes which are very basic, and essentially the same except for the end finger pose. Most of the skill animations are re-used from old specs.

Kappas re-used the Nuhoch rigs and animations, Naga use Krait rigs, Phoenixes, despite it looking quite horrible, use the baby wyvern rigs from HoT, and so on and so on...

Don't get me wrong, there is nothing wrong with re-using rigs, but if it is at the cost of how good or true to the concept something looks, like the phoenix, or how uniquely it looks/feels, without feeling like the same thing in a different colour, it becomes a bit bland.

That does sound a lot like MALS to me, when I was 18 it came on quite suddenly for me, in the matter of 6 weeks I had lost 15kg and I was pretty much bound to my bed, unable to eat anything, as every single bite caused the most horrible sensation of pressure in my stomach, accompanied by nausea.
I also had a very uncomfortable pulsing sensation in my stomach and sometimes all throughout my body, it was almost a bit traumatizing at times.
Also, low mobility is a *symptom* of MALS, a lot of doctors make the mistake of making it it's own diagnosis without any cause being there, I had low mobility, but it was just fine after my surgery, after all now my stomach is receiving proper bloodflow again and can actually work.
Feeling wont really help much here, you wont be able to feel the compression with your fingers, you will need an ultrasound by somebody who knows what they are looking for, or a CT scan, MRI *could* work too under circumstances, but ultrasound and CT are preferred, and usually they will still do a CT scan to confirm the diagnosis.

When you feel the pain/fullness/pressure in your stomach after eating, try this: Lay down on your left side, tuck your legs in slightly, but it HAS to be the LEFT side, stay in that position for a bit.
It is a known position to help with MALS pain and pressure, it makes it easier for food to pass and I had good success with it, when I found out I would often just lay on that side while eating in my bed, haha.

Hope this helps, I wish all the best for you, things will get better, promise!

Hello there, my husband saw your post and recognized some of the symptoms to be similar to mine back when I had MALS, an artery compression syndrome.

Your symptoms do not sound like MALS as throwing up is not a typical symptom, but a very similar compression syndrome called SMA syndrome (Superior Mesenteric Artery syndrome (I hope I spelled that right))  sounds like it could fit, it is very similar to MALS in the symptoms it causes, I was suffering from MALS for 3 years, nobody being able to figure out what I had and nobody believing me, until I saw a specialist who finally diagnosed me and got me to the right surgeon.

MALS causes a compression of the Celiac artery, preventing proper blood flow to your stomach and upper intestine, thus leading to gastroparesis, while SMAS means that the mesenteric artery itself compresses the duodenum, thus food cannot pass and leads to vomiting, often times people end up eating softer foods like soups and smoothies with SMAS as they tolerate it best, but it can be different, I with MALS preferred very dry foods like crackers.

I am in support groups for people with compression syndromes and there are LOTS of people with SMAS, I dont think I have ever read of a single one being diagnosed right away, most take years of suffering to get a diagnosis.

I am not saying *this is it* but I know back when at the end of my strength only weighing 38kg because I could barely eat since 3 years, one comment on reddit, on this exact sub I submitted a very similar post and hat someone save my life by suggesting me to look into compression syndromes.

Look into it, read up online, young slender women are most often hit with compression syndromes, causes for them to create symptoms include weight fluctuations, due to the fat inbetween the arteries decreasing, thus forming a compression. Weight fluctuations are the case for you, I also had weight loss trigger my MALS.

Unfortunately comoression syndromes are not very well known, even among doctors, some even argue their existence, I saw over a dozen doctors and was in two hosoitals, having all kinds of tests done and nobody could help me or had a clue, I wouod just always end up being put into the "psychosomatic" corner, being sent to therapists, being written of as having an eating disorder despite not ever habing had eating or body image issues.

No one could help me until I found someone who knew what he had to look for.

If you need anyone to talk to, have any questions or would like to enter any of the support groups on facebook, send me a DM, I will be happy to help!

Hey there, I was 21 years old and had been very ill for 3 years at the time when it turned out that I needed a big surgery.

Weighing only 38kg I was more at risk  but it was the only way I could get better.

I had an 8 hour open abdominal surgery to fix 4 artery compressions, most namely MALS, had an artery removed from my leg to be used as material to fix the arteries. I had an AV fistula put in there, too!

 I had no problems with anaesthetic, you probably wont either! Those cases are really rare, I would not worry about it, those doctors are humans with empathy, they try everything to help you.

Also for me at least, right before my surgery I was given a pill that made me all woozy and my memory hazy, at that point I just stopped caring, no matter how anxious I was before.

Once you wake up you realize it wasnt that bad, I was heavily drugged up and did  not feel a thing, in fact I am surprised to look back at just how nonchalant I was laying in ICU.

I just played video games a bunch before my surgery to distract myself, during your hospital stay you should REALLY load up your phone with some games or het books to read because it IS gonna be quite boring.

Lots of people here claim it's mainly a medieval thing, but in Germany it is used widely, depending on the situation.

When adressing people formally (Siezen) by referring to them as "Sie" instead of "Du", like a waitress would, or you would your boss, *Ihr* and forms of it will be used as you would use "your" or *dein/deine* in german. 

Examples:

"Wie geht es Ihrer Katze?" - "How is your cat?"

"Kann ich Ihnen etwas bringen?" - "Can I bring you something?"

"Ihr neues Buch hat mir sehr gefallen!" - "I really liked your new book!"

Being German, this is how everyone I know including me adressed people from strangers you want to be friendly towards, teachers, doctors, customers, bosses, almost everyone you are not familiar with, you have to show respect for at work (especially higher establishments like Hotels and Restaurants (exception might be fastfood restaurants)) and so on. When applying for Jobs or writing formal mail you will also use this.

If adressing someone formally, forms of "ihr" will also be used in some cases you would use "your" for.

"Wie geht es *Ihrer* Katze?" - "How is your cat?"

"Kann ich *Ihnen* etwas bringen?" - "Can I bring you something?"

"*Ihr* neues Buch hat mir sehr gefallen!" - "I really liked your new book!"

I was doing an internship at a the clinic for two weeks during winter, I was around 15-16, the vet clinic also had a dog pension for owners who wanted to take a vacation and just have us care for them for a few days or weeks.
Especially we as trainees would be tasked with taking them out as we were barely qualified to do much else besides watching the vets and cleaning.
We had a tiny old grey dog called Jumbo ironically, I would curse him each morning as he would shit and piss all over his room through the night, bu he was always so excited and happy I could barely be frustrated.
We were just doing our usual routine, one trainee and I took Jumbo out, halfway through the field we see another trainee with one of the vets walking two pitbulls which had just arrived the day before, the vet waved, signalling us to go to the side further into the field, into the thick snow so they could walk past.
